h1: Factory Sheds in Pakistan: Steel Buildings for Production Lines and Plants
quickAnswer: A factory shed is a steel building that holds your machines, people and material flow. Steel Mind designs it around your production layout with clear spans, the right height and good light and air.
alt: Interior of a steel factory shed with wide clear span and skylights.

faq.q: What size factory shed can Steel Mind build?
faq.a: Steel Mind has built sheds from a few thousand square feet to almost 100,000 square feet.

faq.q: Can the shed be built while the old one runs?
faq.a: Often yes. The engineer will plan access and safe working zones with you.

blocks.title: What a Factory Shed Must Do

blocks.text: A factory shed must hold your machines, your people and your material flow. It needs clear floor area, enough height, good light and good air. Steel Mind designs the shed around your production layout and not the other way round.

Clear span matters because fewer columns mean more freedom to place machines and move goods. Height should be set from the tallest machine and from any crane or conveyor. Heavy machines may need a stronger floor slab, so share machine weights early. Skylights and ventilators reduce heat and electricity use. The end wall should be planned so that bays can be added later.

Textile and apparel plants, steel processors, packaging units, food plants and assembly lines use steel factory sheds. Clients of Steel Mind include Haier, Imperial Denim and Moiz Steel. For Haier, Steel Mind built a PEB store shed of 32,400 square feet at Raiwind, 30 feet high, 180 feet wide and 180 feet long.

Send the machine list, the floor plan and the site details. The engineer prepares the layout and the 3D model. After you approve it, the factory fabricates the steel and the crews erect it. See One-Step Solution.
